payload.prompt: Registre una nota de gastos de viaje para Paula González (paula.gonzalez@example.org) por "Visita cliente Bergen". El viaje duró 4 días con dietas (tarifa diaria 800 NOK). Gastos: billete de avión 4600 NOK y taxi 250 NOK.

payload.goal: Registrar una nota de gastos de viaje para Paula González por 'Visita cliente Bergen', incluyendo dietas (4 días × 800 NOK), billete de avión (4600 NOK) y taxi (250 NOK).
success_checks: Empleada Paula González existe en el sistema o ha sido creada
Nota de gastos creada con descripción 'Visita cliente Bergen'
Gasto de billete de avión registrado: 4600 NOK
Total de la nota de gastos: 8050 NOK
Estado de la nota de gastos: borrador o enviada para aprobación
risk_notes: No se especifican fechas de inicio y fin del viaje; son campos obligatorios en Tripletex — se deben solicitar o estimar
No se indica si Paula González ya existe como empleada; puede ser necesario crearla primero
La tarifa diaria de 800 NOK debe coincidir con las tarifas configuradas en el sistema (Statens satser u otras); verificar categoría de dieta aplicable
No se especifica si los gastos incluyen IVA; el billete de avión puede estar exento (0% MVA) y el taxi puede tener 25% MVA — requiere confirmación
No se indica método de pago (empresa o empleado); puede afectar el flujo de reembolso
No se adjuntan recibos/comprobantes; Tripletex puede requerirlos para aprobación
payload.suggested_first_action: Verificar si Paula González existe como empleada en Tripletex via GET /employee?email=paula.gonzalez@example.org; si no existe, crearla antes de registrar la nota de gastos.

line_items.description: Billete de avión - Visita cliente Bergen

ordered_steps: 1. GET /employee?email=paula.gonzalez@example.org — verificar si la empleada existe
2. Si no existe: POST /employee — crear empleada Paula González con email paula.gonzalez@example.org
3. Confirmar fechas de inicio y fin del viaje (requeridas para POST /travelExpense)
4. POST /travelExpense — crear nota de gastos con descripción 'Visita cliente Bergen', employeeId obtenido, fechas del viaje
5. POST /travelExpense/cost — registrar dieta: categoría 'dietas', cantidad 4, tarifa 800 NOK/día, total 3200 NOK
6. POST /travelExpense/cost — registrar billete de avión: categoría 'transporte aéreo', importe 4600 NOK, IVA 0%
7. POST /travelExpense/cost — registrar taxi: categoría 'taxi/transporte', importe 250 NOK, IVA 25%
8. Verificar total de la nota: 3200 + 4600 + 250 = 8050 NOK
9. Enviar nota de gastos para aprobación si corresponde: PUT /travelExpense/{id}/:approve

planned_endpoints.summary: Find cost category corresponding with sent data.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.

rules: ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'NO_ACCESS' (safest default — avoids 422 errors). Only use 'STANDARD' if email login is explicitly needed.
startDate is a TOP-LEVEL field on the employee object. Do NOT put it inside an employments array.
dateOfBirth is a TOP-LEVEL field. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
jobTitle is set via PUT /employee/{id} AFTER creation — it cannot be set in the initial POST.
Do NOT include an 'employments' array in POST /employee — employment details go via separate POST /employee/employment endpoint.

For occupation codes (STYRK/yrkeskode): POST /employee/employment first, then GET /employee/employment/occupationCode?nameAndCode=XXXX to find the code, then PUT /employee/employment/details to set it.
ALWAYS include project={"id": project_id} if prompt mentions a project.
Paths must NOT include /v2/ prefix — use /travelExpense not /v2/travelExpense.

payload.headline: Perfect score achieved but 3 validation errors and redundant API calls hurt efficiency
what_went_wrong: POST /travelExpense/perDiemCompensation failed 3 times: first with 'Country not enabled', then 'Spesifiser avreisedato og returdato', then 'Kun reiseregning, ikke ansattutlegg' — per diem via proper endpoint never succeeded
Duplicate GET /travelExpense/costCategory called 3 times and GET /travelExpense/rateCategory called 3 times — same data fetched repeatedly without pagination params
GET /travelExpense/rate called 3 times to check different rate categories (25888, 25886, 25887) — none matched the 800 NOK rate, wasting 3 calls
PUT /travelExpense/11151223 to add travelDetails was ultimately futile since perDiemCompensation still failed; per diem ended up as a regular cost line anyway
what_worked: All 6 scoring checks passed — correct employee, title, amounts (4600+250+3200) all registered successfully
Fallback to POST /travelExpense/cost for per diem (3200 NOK) was a good recovery when perDiemCompensation endpoint failed
what_to_try_next: Skip perDiemCompensation endpoint entirely and register per diem directly as a cost line from the start — saves 3 failed calls + 1 GET + 1 PUT
Use count/from/to params on GET /travelExpense/costCategory and /rateCategory to avoid repeated calls; fetch once with sufficient count
Include travelDetails in the initial POST /travelExpense body to avoid the extra GET + PUT cycle for version retrieval and update
unnecessary_calls: GET /travelExpense/costCategory (2nd and 3rd calls) — same endpoint called 3 times total without different params
GET /travelExpense/rateCategory (2nd and 3rd calls) — same endpoint called 3 times; rate categories don't match 800 NOK anyway
PUT /travelExpense/11151223 — adding travelDetails didn't fix perDiemCompensation; the fallback cost line approach didn't need this update
